summary: No new High or Medium code-level bugs. Every Tier-1-surfaced hotspot was walked to source and cleared as by-design, tool-noise, or an already-catalogued Low/QA echo. Both carryover regression watches (M-04 keccak literals, M-03 decimal-scale direction) HOLD — no drift. The design is defensively coded: CEI is complete on the mint path, the debt hooks floor (never over-credit), and every unbacked-mint direction fails safe toward over-backing.

regressionWatches.detail: All three literals are byte-identical `keccak256("NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook.v1")`: NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook.sol:31 (HOOK_TYPE_ID), NudgeRatchet.sol:31 (EXPECTED_HOOK_TYPE_ID), NudgeRatchetDelayRelease.sol:52 (EXPECTED_HOOK_TYPE_ID). The fail-CLOSED hook-type guard in both NudgeRatchet variants (_dispatch reverts unless hook.hookTypeId()==literal) is intact. No fourth copy of the literal exists to drift.

NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook 1e12 UP-scale (6dp USDC -> 18dp phUSD, ctor-guarded token==6dp); UniboostMintDebtHook dynamic scale=10**(18-d) read from prime decimals (ctor requires d<=18); BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook UNSCALED (USDS is 18dp, prime immutable = sUSDS.asset()). All three multiply-then-divide (floor). No over-mint direction; each matches its dispatcher's guaranteed prime decimals as wired.

findings.newOrEcho: echo (ledger L-09 / profiler A1 / crossCuttingAnomaly A1-M04-asymmetry)
findings.description: Unlike the two NudgeRatchet variants (which fail-CLOSED via a hookTypeId()==literal require in _dispatch), Uniboost._dispatch and BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch perform NO hook-type validation. If the owner leaves/sets the hook to DefaultDispatchHook or any wrong hook via ATokenDispatcherV2.setHook, dispatch still succeeds and moves value (donation split / sUSDS wrap / PSM donation / POL) while accruing ZERO phUSD debt.
findings.attackVector: Reachable ONLY via onlyOwner setHook (or never wiring the real hook). No unprivileged path. UniboostMintDebtHook/BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook expose no hookTypeId(), so the symmetric guard cannot even be added without an interface change.
findings.impact: Fail-OPEN to UNDER-accrual: fewer phUSD minted than backing moved => protocol OVER-backed, never unbacked. Safe direction; breaks debt bookkeeping silently. Honest severity Low (owner footgun, non-catastrophic direction).
findings.clearedAs: known Low; do not escalate — direction is over-backing, and it is owner-configuration-gated

findings.newOrEcho: echo (ledger L-11 / STATIC-014 / profiler MultiPooler scannerNotes)
findings.description: pool(PoolCall[]) forwards Uniboost.pool per row in a loop, all-or-nothing, gated onlyPooler (trusted keeper). If two rows target the same Uniboost/pool, row 1's swaps move the AMM reserves so row 2's operator-precomputed minPairOut/minTargetOut floors are stale, allowing worse execution for row 2 (bounded by its own floors). No shared mutable state in MultiPooler (pure forwarder, holds no funds); each Uniboost.pool is individually nonReentrant.
findings.attackVector: Keeper self-inflicted / MEV-adjacent; bounded by per-row min-outs. Not reachable by an unprivileged actor (onlyPooler).
findings.impact: At worst a self-DoS (batch reverts on unmet floor) or mildly worse LP execution for a duplicated pool. Low.
findings.clearedAs: known Low (L-11); MultiPooler lacking a nonReentrant guard is immaterial (no funds, no shared state, downstream guards present)

findings.description: setRatio uses `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert` with MAX_RATIO=50, so 50 is settable, while NatSpec/const comment says 'strictly < MAX_RATIO' / 'exclusive upper bound, max settable MAX_RATIO-1'. UniboostMintDebtHook:97 and BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook:78. DEFAULT_RATIO is already 50 (== the cap), so the code and default agree; only the doc comment is wrong.
findings.attackVector: None. Owner-only setter; the only effect is the debt-ratio ceiling being 50% inclusive rather than 49% inclusive.
findings.impact: Cosmetic. Max debt is 50% of dispatched amount either way (well under a 1:1 backing). No security consequence. QA.
findings.clearedAs: QA doc fix (align comments to inclusive-50 or change guard to >=). Not a security finding.

findings.description: gemAmt = (usdsAmount*WAD)/(conv*(WAD+tout)) then usdsSpent = gemAmt*conv*(WAD+tout)/WAD. The divide-before-multiply is INTENTIONAL and faithfully mirrors makerdao/dss-lite-psm buyGem math: it computes the max gem (6dp USDC) affordable from the available USDS, then the exact USDS the PSM will pull for that gem. Proof usdsSpent <= usdsAmount always holds (gemAmt is floored), so the forceApprove(usdsSpent) never exceeds balance. Floor sends sub-unit dust to the protocol (never over-credits), require(gemAmt>0) rejects dust rounding-to-zero, and the whole call is try/catch-isolated so any revert just parks the USDS.
findings.attackVector: None. Self-gated (msg.sender==address(this)), atomic rollback via try/catch in _dispatch.
findings.impact: None. No fund loss, no accounting drift; donation is to an external sink and debt accrues on GROSS amount regardless of donation outcome.

findings.description: Ignored returns walked to source and cleared: (a) IERC4626.deposit shares (218) — pool() later reads the actual sUSDS balanceOf, so the share count is not needed; (b) ISkyPSM.buyGem (260) — USDC is delivered straight to batchMinter (external sink), no local accounting depends on it; (c) IBalancerVault.unlock (274) — the callback returns "" by design; (d) settle (308) — the Balancer V3 transfer->addLiquidity->settle ordering is a valid pay-the-debt pattern and slippage is enforced by params.minBptAmountOut=minBPT inside addLiquidity, with actualInVault measured by balance delta; (e) Uniboost swapExactTokensForTokens (221/234) — amounts-out are re-read via balanceOf for the next leg and each swap has an explicit min-out floor, addLiquidity checks liquidity>=minLP. All value-moving external calls use SafeERC20 (revert-on-false).
findings.attackVector: None; POL/donation paths are owner/keeper-gated and each has an independent slippage floor or balance re-read.
findings.impact: None. No share-accounting mismatch, no silent shortfall that reaches user funds.
findings.clearedAs: tool noise; SafeERC20 + balance-delta + min-out floors cover the paths

findings.description: NFTMinterV2 has no nonReentrant guard and _mint fires onERC1155Received on an attacker-chosen recipient. Walked the CEI ordering: config.price is grown (188) BEFORE dispatch (191), and dispatch(nonReentrant) plus _mint(196) both complete their state effects before/at the callback. A re-entrant mint() from the receiver hook is a fresh, fully-paid mint at the ALREADY-grown price — the attacker gains nothing (no stale-price read, no double-dispatch, no free NFT) and must supply their own approved tokens (safeTransferFrom is from msg.sender). Cross-contract reentry into a DIFFERENT dispatcher during BalancerPoolerV2/PSM/sUSDS external calls also fails: the reentering party (sUSDS/PSM, both trusted) holds no approved prime, so safeTransferFrom reverts. mintFor is authorized-minter-only (trusted).
findings.attackVector: No economic reentrancy. Receiver-hook revert only self-DoSes the caller's own chosen recipient.
findings.impact: None. Price is monotonically grown pre-callback; no read-only reentrancy surface (NFTMinterV2 exposes no price view consumed as an oracle by another contract).
findings.clearedAs: CEI complete before hook; benign per full reentrancy-class checklist

reentrancyChecklist.classic-single-fn: cleared — mint path grows price + completes dispatch (nonReentrant) before _mint callback
reentrancyChecklist.cross-contract A-B-A: cleared — dispatcher.dispatch is nonReentrant; reentry into NFTMinterV2.mint for another dispatcher needs approved prime the trusted callee (sUSDS/PSM/router) does not hold, so safeTransferFrom reverts
reentrancyChecklist.cross-function sibling: cleared — NFTMinterV2's only value state (config.price) is CEI-clean; burn/mintFor are access-gated; no shared stale-balance read
reentrancyChecklist.read-only reentrancy: cleared — no public view of this suite is consumed as a price/exchange-rate oracle by another in-scope contract; getIdealBPT is non-view but not an oracle (staticcall would revert), documented
reentrancyChecklist.ERC1155-receive: cleared — CODE-006: state finalized before onERC1155Received; re-entry is a fresh paid mint
reentrancyChecklist.ERC777 hooks: n/a — primes are USDC/USDS (no tokensReceived hooks); FOT tolerated via balance-delta actualReceived

nonReentrant-not-first-modifier (STATIC-022): benign — the preceding modifiers (onlyAuthorizedPooler/whenNotPaused/onlyOwnerOrRecipient) are pure access/pause checks with no external calls, so running them outside the lock cannot enable reentrancy.
constructor state-after-external-call (STATIC-002/003/004/005): constructor context, no deployed code to re-enter; the external reads (asset()/decimals()) are to trusted tokens.
single-step Ownable (STATIC-024): QA hardening note; owner trusted per Law 3.
